name: Bushing current transformer
summary: Toroidal CT mounted around a transformer or breaker bushing, often with a tapped multi-ratio secondary.
description: A bushing CT is a toroidal core and secondary slipped over the bushing of a power transformer, generator or dead-tank circuit breaker. The bushing conductor is the primary, and several CTs may be stacked on one bushing for differential, overcurrent and metering duties.

Bushing CTs are often multi-ratio, with taps on the secondary, and only the selected tap should be wired to the relay. The symbol shows the location at the bushing, so the reader must check which side of the breaker or transformer the CT sits on to understand the protection zone overlap.
readingNotes: Identify which side of the device each bushing CT sits on.
Check the selected tap on multi-ratio CTs.
drawingChecklist: State selected tap and full ratio
Show position relative to the breaker or winding
distinction: A bushing CT uses the bushing conductor as its primary; a free-standing CT has its own insulated primary.
